# A Short History Times are rough and counted back from today, the way spacers tell them.
## A century ago: the Corporate War Nanotrasen and the Syndicate went to war, and the war ate them both. Nanotrasen was destroyed and the Syndicate broken. One badly damaged Syndicate battle group fled into an uncharted sector and died there. The Phaethon Dynasty, an imperial house that had ruled those worlds for longer than anyone outside them knew, found the wrecks and built a future out of them.
## A century to fifty years ago: the Confederacy In the vacuum Nanotrasen left, the Confederacy, a small government from Sol, seized corporate technology and built it into its fleets. Within fifty years it held more than half the galaxy, and it hunted down whatever the Syndicate had left behind.
## Fifty years ago: the schism Harsh laws drove the great workers' unions to break away as the United Soviet Socialist Planets. The Confederacy reformed as the [textlink="Trans-Solarian Federation" link="TSFMC_Entry"] and fought to bring them back. It won the civil war that followed.
## Forty years ago: Colossus In the peace, scouts reached the sector now called Colossus. They found worlds rich beyond reason, anomalies nobody could explain, a Dynasty that had been there all along, and that they could not leave. Every ship that has tried since has turned back or been lost. People came anyway, and never stopped coming. A trade company built [textlink="Caelestinus Central" link="Caelestinus"] to shelter them, under the guns of TSF and USSP garrisons.
## Thirty years ago: neutrality The Federation tried to rule the sector's trade and ban the Syndicate technology that had spread through it. Caelestinus cut its ties with the TSF and declared itself neutral. It has stayed that way.
## Five years ago: the war comes back The TSF and the USSP fell out over who should govern Colossus, and the civil war reignited here, almost half a century after it ended. The [textlink="Phaethon Dynasty" link="PDV_Entry"], who call the sector their holy land, armed insurgents against both. Federation contractors sent to secure the colonies saw how the war was fought, laid down their contracts, and came to Caelestinus to guard it.
## Three years ago: the Invasion The Federation crushed the insurgents and drove most of the [textlink="USSP" link="USSP_Entry"] out. Then it turned on the Dynasty. The largest fleet it ever sent into Colossus came in behind the battleship [italic]Halcyon[/italic], to take the Dynasty's worlds and keep them. The Dynasty stepped into the open as the Vanguard and met it. The Federation called the war that followed a pacification. The Dynasty calls it the Invasion, and still does.
## Last year: the Collapse After two years, neither side had won. Then [textlink="Kyphrus collapsed" link="WGLoreCollapse"] into a black hole, and [textlink="the Unmooring" link="WGLoreUnmooring"] came in from the edge of the sector like a tide. Most of the Federation fleet was out there, strung along the sector's edge on its way to Dynasty worlds. Its ships fell silent one by one. A few came back months later with crews who swore they had been gone an hour. Most never came back at all. When it was over, the Federation's navy in Colossus was the [italic]Halcyon[/italic] and a handful of capital patrols.
## The Long Night Six pillars that Nanotrasen's first survey had logged and forgotten began to wake as [textlink="the Lattice" link="WGLoreLattice"]. They did not wake together. For forty days the hexagon had gaps, and the Unmooring came in through them. Federation engineers and Vanguard artificers, who had been shooting at each other the week before, built braces and relays around the sleeping pillars and fed them power until they answered. The [italic]Halcyon[/italic]'s foundries never stopped.
Through all forty days, the inner worlds held. Clocks agreed. Compasses pointed. The Vanguard says [textlink="the Sultan" link="WGLoreSultan"] held them. Nobody has offered a better explanation.
When the sixth pillar woke, the Unmooring stopped exactly at the edge of their reach. The war did not end with a treaty. It simply stopped.
## Months ago: the Caelestinus Accord Nobody would live in a world that one navy could switch off. The Federation and the Dynasty signed [textlink="the Caelestinus Accord" link="WGLoreAccord"], giving the anchors and the station to a third party sworn to neither. The station's guards became [textlink="the Bench" link="WGLoreJudges"], and the [textlink="Common Writ" link="WGCommonWrit"] became the sector's law. Both sides agreed to set the war aside until reality is safe. Both sides know what that means.
## Now Federation transports still dock at the [italic]Halcyon[/italic], carrying fresh marines, and nobody outside the Federation knows [textlink="where they come from" link="WGLoreReinforcements"]. The [textlink="Reavers" link="WGLoreReavers"] rise from the people the sector broke. The [textlink="ADS" link="WGLoreAds"] wakes in the dark. Hives stir under Aerumna, and Chimera flesh drifts in on dead ships. Past the anchors, someone is singing.
If the Lattice falls, everyone dies, whatever flag they fly. This is where you play.
